chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about something from the expiation for an oath, so he said: 'He should fast for three days.' I said, 'He is weak from fasting and is unable (to do it).' He said: 'He should give charity to ten poor people.' I said, 'He is unable to do that.' He said: 'So let him seek forgiveness of Allah and not repeat it, for it is the best of the expiations, and its maximum and its minimum. So let him seek forgiveness of his Lord and display repentance and remorse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking an oath if one cannot fast or feed the poor?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a graded hierarchy for expiating broken oaths, culminating in istighfar (seeking forgiveness) as both the minimum and maximum penalty for those unable to fast or feed the poor. Shia scholars highlight the unique designation of istighfar as the 'best' expiation, emphasizing that sincere repentance (tawbah) with remorse (nadamah) holds profound spiritual weight, potentially surpassing material acts like feeding the needy in terms of divine acceptance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about something from en expiation for the oath. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should Fast for three days’. I said, ‘He is weak from the Fasting and is frustrated (from doing it)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should give in charity to ten poor ones’. I said, ‘He is frustrated from that’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So let him seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and he should not repeat it, for it is the best of the expiations, and the most economical, and lowest of it. So let him seek Forgiveness of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and display his repentance, and his remorse’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the Kaffarah (expiation) due to oath. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is fasting for three days.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if one feels weak and cannot do it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He can give charity to ten destitute people.’ I asked, ‘What happens if he cannot do it?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He must ask forgiveness from Allah and must not do such thing again because the best is Kaffarah (expiation) in its highest and lowest form, so he must ask forgiveness from his Lord and express regret and repentance.’”
